Subject: Initial capacity questionnaire and next steps

Hi Samir — great to meet yesterday. Thanks for walking through the Cedarholm Q3 rollout window. As promised, attaching a short capacity questionnaire to capture traffic shape and SLAs so we can produce a properly sized Dedicated proposal.

Quick asks:
- Can you confirm peak concurrent RPS and 95th/99th token latency targets for the inference calls?
- What percent of requests are chat (interactive) vs. batch embed/ret-rank?
- Expected daily token volume and peak burst multiplier (if known).

We usually propose a base reserved slab sized for steady-state + a small shoulder pool for predictable bursts, plus an ephemeral burst band for exceptional events. I attached the questionnaire (cedarholm_capacity_questionnaire.pdf).

Proposed short timeline:
- You complete questionnaire by Tue (15th)
- We return initial sizing matrix by Thu (17th)
- Align on SLA/eviction policy and add into SOW the following week

Best,

From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Cedarholm traffic + initial sizing notes (internal)

Forwarding Samir's traffic details — key numbers above. Draft thoughts below (please review and adjust):

Sizing heuristics (first pass):
- Baseline reserved slab to cover 95% of steady-state: ~40 A100-equivalent GPU slots (model family: Llama-v3-13B quantized path).
- Shoulder pool: +8 GPU slots to handle routine marketing spikes (this is billed as reserved but lower-cost shoulder tier).
- Ephemeral burst band: +10 slots that are preemptible and charged on burst usage; evictable under platform pressure.

Policy recommendations:
- Autoscale window: 90s rolling; cold-start warmup via KV cache priming for canary nodes.
- Preemption fallback: route heavier requests to a smaller model slice (7B) with degraded-quality flag; this preserves latency SLOs for interactive flows.
- Crediting: provide burst-credit bucket for first 200k tokens per month of ephemeral use; beyond that billable at burst-rate.
- Eviction priority: ephemeral > shoulder > baseline. In the SOW we'll include explicit throttling thresholds and a hard failover to smaller models at 70% cluster pressure.

Open Qs for Samir we should confirm before proposal:
- Tolerance for degraded model quality during preemption?
- Which regions do you want pinned? (us-west primary / eu secondary?)

Ben — can you run a quick cost simulation (A100-equivalent hours) for the above and return numbers by EOD? Laura — I'll draft the matrix for Samir once we have costs.

—Alex

Subject: Dedicated capacity matrix & operational controls (proposal)

Samir — thanks for the quick data. Please find the attached Dedicated Capacity Matrix (dedicated_capacity_matrix_20270614.xlsx). Key elements from the proposal summarized below so you can present to procurement:

1) Capacity composition (monthly commitment):
- Baseline reserved: 40 GPU slots (steady-state SLA coverage)
- Shoulder reserved: 8 GPU slots (short-term predictable spikes)
- Ephemeral burst band: up to 10 preemptible slots (on-demand)

2) Autoscale and safety controls:
- Autoscale cadence: evaluate every 30–90s with scale step = 2 slots; progressive backoff on scale-down to avoid thrashing.
- Canary scaling: new nodes are added behind a canary pool (10% of new capacity) for 5–10 minutes to validate KV priming and latency before full routing.
- Failover routing: when cluster pressure >70%, flow-level fallback to 7B model variant for non-critical calls (explicit opt-in in SDK).

3) Billing & credits:
- Ephemeral bursts consumed under the burst band are billed at a higher per-hour rate; first 200k tokens/month waived as burst-credit during first three months of the contract.
- Shoulder is reserved capacity at a ~15% discount vs baseline reserved pricing.

4) Eviction & guardrails:
- Eviction order: ephemeral -> shoulder -> baseline.
- Hard SLO breach threshold triggers a region-failover to eu-west (if enabled in SOW).
- Telemetry: token-level latency histograms, per-model error rates; 30-day retention by default, extended retention available as add-on.

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_matrix_20270614.xlsx (xlsx)

Action items for you:
- Confirm whether Cedarholm wants automatic fallback to smaller models (we'll add opt-in flag in SDK)
- Confirm preferred region pinning (us-west only, or us-west + eu-west DR)
- Procurement: we'll include the burst-credit language in the commercial term sheet; if you want an escrow for credits, flag and we'll add allocation mechanics.

If that looks good I can convert these bullets into SOW language and route to legal/procurement.

Regards,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 14:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity matrix & operational controls (proposal)

Alex — thanks for the clear matrix. A few clarifications from our side:

- We accept the baseline + shoulder + ephemeral composition. Good to have the burst-credit for onboarding.
- We would like automatic fallback to the 7B variant for non-critical conversational flows; please include this as an opt-out flag for us (default ON).
- Region pinning: start with us-west primary, add eu-west as passive DR (only activated during sustained >20% latency degradation for >10 minutes).
- Procurement request: can you include a short clause that guarantees a maximum window for forced preemption notices (e.g., a 60-second advisory before large-scale eviction) so our on-call can act?

Also, can you send the finalized SOW and commercial term sheet (we'll need DocuSign). We'll route to legal once we have the wording for burst credits and the preemption advisory window.

Thanks — Samir
